blindSummary:
Trans visitors face significant risk here. The penal code criminalises "unnatural acts" (up to 5 years, applied to both men and women), enforcement is active (periodic arrest waves), and anti-LGBT forces are pushing to raise sentences to 15 years. Mob violence against perceived LGBT people is documented, and even public discussion is policed: two men were jailed in 2024 on "false news" charges after accusing the head of government of tolerating homosexuality. There is no legal gender recognition and no visible community infrastructure — queer life in the capital is deeply underground.

For a visitor: visible trans presentation risks arrest and mob violence.
blindOutOfScope: Same-sex criminalisation is the statutory vehicle; mob violence is documented climate.
blindSourceSummaries: International legal-aid trust country profile: this country criminalises same-sex sexual activity (a provision of the 1965 penal code, up to 5 years' imprisonment). (Only the opening of the profile was retrievable at fetch time.)

Anti-criminalisation news platform (July 2024): anti-LGBT forces in this country seek longer prison time - after the head of government alleged homosexuality is 'tolerated', a legislator proposed a bill mirroring a failed 2022 initiative raising sentences to 10-15 years for 'offences of bisexuality [including homosexuality], transsexuality, necrophilia and zoophilia' plus fines of up to millions in local currency; abuses against LGBT+ people are commonplace.

Foreign public broadcaster (June 2024): two men jailed in this country for 'spreading false news' after accusing the head of government of tolerating homosexuality - an activist and a prominent religious leader received three months and fines; the head of government had said homosexuality was 'not accepted, but tolerated' after a foreign politician expressed support for same-sex marriage at a student forum in the capital.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on this country: documents preelectoral violence, torture, and 'violence and discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) persons' among major human-rights problems.

Anti-criminalisation news platform (Sept 2018): a wave of politically motivated anti-gay arrests as the 2019 election approached - two women and two men detained in the capital for 'acts against the order of nature'; a local LGBT organisation warned that 'the hunt for sexual minorities begins' as the government defended itself against 'pro-homosexual' accusations; a regional LGBT body called for accountability.

Local daily (Nov 2023): a man's body was exhumed and set on fire in the street after locals found out he was gay - a case that shocked this country, where homosexuality is punishable with prison time.
blindTangential: “Unnatural acts” criminalised (up to 5 years, both sexes) — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
